title: Adder-DCIM: A Parallel Bit-Flexible Digital CIM Accelerator Joint Model Compression Framework for AdderNet Inference
problem: Digital CIM accelerators face power and area overhead from multiplication, difficulty in exploiting fine-grained sparsity, and throughput degradation from bit-serial architecture, especially for edge deployment.
motivation: Edge AI requires low-power, low-latency, low-cost accelerators; digital CIM offers promise but faces practical efficiency challenges.
method: Adder-DCIM compresses the neural network by breaking operations into simpler forms, removing unnecessary computations (fine-grained sparsity), and using fewer bits where precision isn't critical—with KLD validation ensuring accuracy is preserved. It then runs this on hardware that performs calculations directly in memory with parallel processing instead of serial bit-by-bit operations, supporting different precision levels throughout. A flexible circuit efficiently handles these varying precisions, and the hardware replaces multiplication with addition to reduce power consumption and silicon area.
key_novelty: The core innovation is co-designing the neural network and a parallel in-memory computing accelerator with flexible precision handling so the network replaces multiplication with addition while maintaining accuracy.
contributions: CIM-friendly model compression framework with operator decomposition and lossless sparsity
Synchronous parallel DCIM architecture for throughput improvement
Bit-flexible minimal selector circuit for mixed-precision computation

metrics.speedup: 20.7× improvement in energy efficiency × throughput density for ResNet50
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 134 TOPS/W peak; 255 TOPS/W@4.2bit, 243 TOPS/W@4.4bit ResNet inference
metrics.area: 6.49 TOPS/mm² peak throughput density at INT8
metrics.accuracy: 0.34% loss on CIFAR10 ResNet20, 0.7% on ImageNet ResNet50

limitations: Evaluation limited to CNNs (ResNet); transformer and other neural network architectures not evaluated.
